issues.legal_issue: The market value of acquired land may be assessed using a nearby resale as a comparable when other valuation evidence is inadequate, with an adjustment for the difference in size between the comparable parcel and the acquired land.
material_facts: The acquired land comprised a large area, and much of the sale evidence concerned land too far away to be useful.
A purchaser of a plot near the acquired land resold it at a higher price shortly before the acquisition notification.
The Land Acquisition Officer had not based the award on a particular sale document, and the evidence supporting the other valuation findings was also inadequate.
The acquired land was substantially larger than the nearby plot used as the comparable.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in relying wholly on the Land Acquisition Officer’s award. The nearby resale was the safest available guide, and compensation of Rs. 2.50 per square yard was reasonable after accounting for the larger area of the acquired land.
issues.legal_principle: In assessing market value, a sale of nearby land close to the valuation date may provide a basis for compensation when other evidence is inadequate. The difference between a small comparable plot and a large acquired area must be taken into account. The judgment refers to the Hyderabad Land Acquisition Act and notes that its Section 3(1) corresponds to Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; it relies on no earlier cases for this valuation approach.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and nearby_comparable_resale and resale_near_valuation_time and large_acquired_extent

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.nearby_comparable_resale: A parcel near the acquired land was resold, providing evidence of its value.
predicates.resale_near_valuation_time: The resale occurred close to the time at which the acquired land’s value had to be assessed.
predicates.large_acquired_extent: The acquired area was substantially larger than the parcel used as the comparable.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-compensation appeal has a nearby resale close to the valuation time and the acquired area is larger than the comparable parcel, compensation is assessed by adjusting the comparable sale for the difference in extent.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for acquired land is to carry solatium and interest running from the taking of possession.
material_facts: The court fixed compensation for the acquired land.
Possession of the acquired land had been taken.
The trial court had awarded solatium and interest, and the Supreme Court directed that the usual additions be made to the compensation it fixed.
issues.conclusion: The compensation is to include solatium at 15% and interest at 6% from the date possession was taken.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the usual additions of solatium and interest to the compensation award. It cited no specific statutory provision or earlier case for this direction.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.compensation_awarded: The court has determined compensation for the acquired land.
predicates.possession_taken: Possession of the acquired land has been taken.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-compensation appeal results in a compensation award and possession has been taken, solatium and interest from possession are awarded.
